New England Patriots starting left tackle Will Campbell suffered a knee injury during this past Sunday's Week 5 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Campbell underwent MRI testing to determine the severity of his injury on Monday. And according to a report from NFL insider Tom Pelissero, the 22-year-old offensive lineman avoided a serious, long-term injury. Campbell is now considered "week-to-week" as the Patriots prepare for this coming Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the division-rival New York Jets. “We’ll see how the week goes,” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said of Campbell's injury status on Monday. “It’ll get looked at and continues to rehab. Wasn’t able to finish the game, so I don’t know how much time he’ll miss — if he’ll be back towards the end of the week, if he’ll be back Wednesday. We’ll take it day by day and see how he feels tomorrow, see what he does Wednesday, and keep you updated on the injury report.” After a slow start to the 2026 season, the Patriots are beginning to catch their stride. Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders marked the team's second consecutive victory and third win of the season thus far. Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Jets will kick off at 1 p.m. ET.

home.headline: Former Longhorn D'Shawn Jamison signs with New England Patriots
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: While Jamison is still trying to carve out a role in the NFL, he was impressive during his time as a Longhorn. In 47 games in the burnt orange, he had 139 total tackles and six interceptions. During that stretch, Jamison also got some playing time on special teams, excelling regardless of the role. With injuries mounting, the New England Patriots have added depth . On Wednesday, they signed former Longhorn D'Shawn Jamison to their practice squad. The Houston native will have to battle for a roster spot, but he brings experience to the table and will now look to make his mark in New England. Since making his NFL debut in 2023, Jamison has appeared in 18 games with the Steelers and the Panthers. The 27-year-old has spent most of his time on special teams, returning three punts for 60 yards. During the 2023 campaign, he got some action on defense, making 10 total tackles in 15 games. Now that Jamison has a new home, he can focus on fighting his way onto the game-day roster. That won't be easy, as the Patriots have a crowded cornerback room, making his most realistic path to suiting up at Gillette Stadium on Sundays on special teams. However, that is a challenge he is ready to tackle. Although Jamison will have to learn a new system, he is now with an organization that has had a good track record of developing players who have excelled on special teams at other stops. He will not be the only new face on the practice squad as the Patriots also signed RB Hassan Haskins. home.headline: Patriots vs. Jets preview for NFL Week 6
home.blurb: The Jets’ offense, meanwhile, has had its issues and has been unable to perform at the same level as its defensive counterpart. The group has limited its own errors as evidenced by its three giveaways all year, but it nonetheless ranks in the bottom half of the league in most other major categories. While three straight losses to NFC North opponents turned a 1-0 start into a 1-3 record, the Jets are entering a crucial meeting with the Patriots off of their most impressive win thus far. Sure, their offense scored only 17 points and fumbled twice, but their defense registered eight sacks, two fumble recoveries of its own, and limited what was a 3-1 Browns team to a mere 198 yards of offense and 3.0 yards per play. In the kicking game, Austin McNamara has gotten plenty of work in: he leads the league with 25 punts. Jason Sanders, meanwhile, is a combined 15 of 17 on field goals and extra points. Isaiah Williams is averaging a very good 10.9 yards per punt return. The Jets’ reserve lists include one of their first-round draft picks this year, wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. The 30th overall pick in this year’s draft suffered an ankle injury in Week 1. Like the Patriots’ A.J. Brown, he too returned to practice on Wednesday to open his 21-day window to return to the active roster. Sunday’s game between the New England Patriots and New York Jets will be a meeting between two second-year head coaches who have enjoyed differing levels of success so far. Whereas Mike Vrabel led the Patriots to the Super Bowl in his first season and appears to have his team firing on all cylinders again in 2026, Aaron Glenn went just 3-14 in Year 1 and is also currently the owner of a losing record. That said, could it be that the Jets are quietly building a contender? There are some arguments for it, so let’s take a closer look at the 2-3 team before its trip to face the 3-2 Patriots. The Jets are currently below .500 and outside the AFC playoff picture , but a look at their statistics reveals that there are some areas of their team that can compete with any other in football. If we look solely at the statistics as presented, one could expect a fairly defensive-dominated battle between two of the best such units in football. The Jets’ is indeed just that, and well-rounded despite being in the middle of the pack in the turnover category (that said, the group did caught its first interception since 2024 earlier this year). That being said, New England’s offense — which scored 74 points over the last two games — is as formidable an opponent as it has faced thus far. For the first time since 2023, the Jets opened a season with a win again. However, the momentum they built in Week 1 quickly started to fade again: the club lost three straight afterwards. picks.headline: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants
picks.blurb: Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Saints Rookie Report: Week 6 preview vs. the Giants NEW ORLEANS, LA - OCTOBER 11: Lorenzo Styles Jr. #36 of the New Orleans Saints plays against the Minnesota Vikings during the first half of a game at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026, in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Derick Hingle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Caleb Yaccarino Wed, October 14, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads I want to start this week's report by talking about this class. Like many, I have seen it ranked very low on lists of the best and worst classes from 2026. I don't disagree with those lists, and really, who can? Injuries, players being behind veterans, or some still needing to develop have kept this class from doing much, but you shouldn't lose faith in this group. The players who have been in the game have made plays that are good starting points, and although development matters, it's not like those players have been bad. Jordyn Tyson's injury is annoying to say the least, but hopefully we can forget about that once he's back. Do I think this class is going to be like 2025? No, but in hindsight, I think he could be a nice, middle-of-the-road draft class. Now onto the players: DT Christen Miller Finally, Christen Miller was able to get into the game on Sunday, and eventhough the Saints could not win, he did well in his short time. Miller made big plays against the run, took up blocks from offensive linemen to open up holes for other defensive linemen and the linebackers to stop the run, and in my opinion, proved he should be the starting nose tackle. It wasn't perfect, but it was enough for the Saints to play him more. This should hopefully be the case against the New York Giants, and to stop RB Cam Skattebo, you need a big defensive lineman that can prevent him from carrying the pile. TE Oscar Delp With the Vikings sending blitzes nearly every play, Delp had to step up as a blocker, and he did. The Giants are also at the top of the league in blitz rate, so Delp will be a primary blocker once again. I do hope the Saints utilize him as a receiver, because Noah Fant has had pre-snap issues this season, and prioritizing youth should be the plan moving forward. Try something new. OG Jeremiah Wright Speaking of trying something new, I wish Jeremiah Wright would get some snaps, but now that pressure is on the organization to win, a Cesar Ruiz trade feels less likely due to the risk. If a coaching change is made, I hope the next staff will give Wright a chance. WR Bryce Lance Last week, I said that it's clear Lance is not ready for WR3, and the Vikings game only reinforced that. The Saints need to make the move and put him at WR4 moving forward so he can learn. I know I have said to prioritize youth, but I also want to prioritize Tyler Shough's development, and Lance is negatively affecting that. WR Barion Brown Brown is a similar spot to Lance, but it's also clear he needs to figure out the return game as well. His fellow former LSU Tiger, Zavion Thomas, is in nearly the exact same spot with the Bears, but due to their offensive struggles with Caleb Williams being out, they have begun to utilize Thomas more. In addition, Thomas has improved as their main return man. Hopefully, the same can happen for Brown. RB CJ Donaldson Donaldson was thrown to the wolves trying to block the Vikings blitz, and although I felt he did a decent job, he did have a holding call on one of the plays. As a rusher, Donaldson did exactly what I thought, picking up tough yards that did help the Saints in their run game. Against the Giants, I want him to be included once again. OT Mason Murphy In probably the most confusing moment of the game, which is saying a lot, the Saints put in Mason Murphy on a random drive, then subbed him out for Asim Richards the next. At first, I thought Richards got injured, but Moore said after the game that it was planned. I actually thought Richards did better than usual, and Murphy wasn't great when he came in. I don't think the Saints will make this substitution again. DB Lorenzo Styles Jr. Styles Jr. was back last game, which was nice to see, but his involvement was limited. I wouldn't be shocked if that changes after Jayden Price's release being cut, so Styles Jr. could be the return man next to Brown against the Giants. Injured players: WR Jordyn Tyson

away.headline: Saints WR Chris Olave appears on injury report with new issue
away.blurb: Olave took the field for practice in a limited capacity on Thursday, but a new “foot” designation was added to the report. While this “foot” designation could be cause for concern, the fact that Olave took the field for a limited practice is a positive sign for his Week 5 status. New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave did not participate in Wednesday’s Week 5 practice session, landing on the injury report with a “rest” designation. This new issue comes as a surprise to fans and reporters who saw Olave take a hit to the knee late in Monday night’s matchup against the Atlanta Falcons. Trailing 45-17 with just over one minute remaining in the primetime contest, the superstar wide receiver limped off the field with what was assumed to be a knee injury. Olave ranks second in NFL receiving yards so far this season with 491, trailing only Dallas Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb (498). He recorded his third 100+ receiving yard game of the year in Monday’s loss to the Falcons, reeling in eight receptions for 116 yards. The 1-3 Saints will welcome the Minnesota Vikings for a Week 5 matchup this coming Sunday. away.headline: Who's in, who's out? Breaking down the Saints-Vikings injury report
away.blurb: LB Anfernee Jennings (knee) also did not practice this week and will not dress out against the Vikings. He's an underrated defender against the run and we saw just how badly the team missed him on Monday night. OL Jeremiah Wright (concussion) couldn't finish practice on Thursday and didn't return to the field on Friday while following the NFL's concussion protocol. The rookie right guard has a bright future so it's important to give him time to heal up. The Minnesota Vikings ruled out starting left tackle Christian Darrisaw (concussion) and cornerback Charles Demmings (hamstring). They do still have another week for him to practice while remaining on injured reserve before reactivating him. But you have to wonder how patient they'll be with Kaden Elliss unavailable. away.headline: Vikings-Saints Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, some intrigue with a number of players listed as questionable, including Jordan Addison, Justin Jefferson, and Brian O’Neill. I’m gonna go out on a limb and say that all three will play on Sunday. I know they will be cautious with all of them, but it doesn’t sound like Jefferson has experienced any problems with his ankle all week. It sounds like Addison and O’Neill’s injuries are more of the minor variety they will play through. It’s not a surprise at this point that Christian Darrisaw is out, as he hadn’t practiced all week. He should be ready to go after the bye week. For the Saints, Alvin Kamara is questionable but my guess is he’ll play on Sunday. Safety Julian Blackmon is also questionable but probably will play as well. Those are the two key players on the Saints list this week. Everyone else is either listed as out or do not have a deisignation and/or are a backup. Who will be sitting this one out? Saints WR Chris Olave absent from New Orleans practice ahead of Giants clash - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Saints WR Chris Olave absent from New Orleans practice ahead of Giants clash Josh Davis, ClutchPoints Wed, October 14, 2026 at 11:34 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave missed Wednesday's practice due to an illness as the team prepares for Sunday's Week 6 road matchup vs. the New York Giants. The Saints listed the former Ohio State standout as a non-participant on Wednesday's injury report, leaving his status for Sunday's matchup uncertain. Meanwhile, New Orleans hopes to bounce back from a 23-13 Week 5 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Olave recorded four receptions for 46 yards in that defeat, and the Saints will continue monitoring their leading receiver as preparations for the Giants continue. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) NewOrleans.Football's Mike Triplett shared both teams' Wednesday injury reports on X, formerly Twitter, confirming Olave's absence alongside several other Saints players dealing with injuries and illnesses. Meanwhile, Olave wasn't the only New Orleans player sidelined Wednesday. Linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf), edge rusher Anfernee Jennings (knee) and defensive tackle Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed practice. However, quarterback Tyler Shough practiced fully despite appearing on the injury report with a left-hand issue. Long snapper Zach Wood (calf) and guard Jeremiah Wright (concussion) also participated fully. New Orleans will release additional practice reports Thursday and Friday before traveling to MetLife Stadium for Sunday's matchup. For now, the Saints have not assigned Olave a game-status designation, leaving his Week 6 availability unresolved following Wednesday's illness-related absence. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 6 schedule, including five locks against the spread Getty Images I don't know what it is about the Week 6 slate, but I think we're going to have some underdogs bark rather loudly. I have four underdogs not only finding their way into my five locks of the week, but also two of them pulling off outright upsets. Judging by the headline of this article, you already know that the Panthers are one of those dogs that I think will win in Week 6 as they head up to Philly to face the Eagles . While I'll get into why I feel that way below, I'm just as fascinated by what may happen if it comes to fruition. Would this be the straw that breaks the camel's back when it comes to Nick Sirianni's job? Or does he live to fight another day and gear up for a do-or-die NFC East showdown in primetime with the Cowboys in Week 7? Either way, the storylines that could flow out of this upcoming slate feel like they're as juicy as we've seen so far this season, and that's saying something. Anyways, I'll look to improve upon my picks after a lackluster Week 5 where I went 2-3 ATS with my five locks of the week, along with 6-9 ATS and 9-5-1 SU for the overall slate. Note : Cincinnati, Detroit, Miami and Minnesota are on the bye in Week 6. Locks of the Week ATS : 12-12-1 ATS : 33-44-2 Carolina Panthers at Philadelphia Eagles Sunday, 1 p.m. (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ ) Carolina comes into this matchup with a pretty sizable rest advantage over Philadelphia. On top of the Panthers coming off of the bye, the Eagles were just in London last week. So, we have one team extremely well rested, while the other is reeling and just came off a demoralizing international loss. Beyond the lopsided rest advantage, the Eagles just feel like a mess right now. They're bottom five in the league in points per game (18.4), yards per game (262.2), and passing yards per game (170.6) coming into Week 6. Sure, some of that can be attributed to injury, but even when they've had their full squad, it's been clunky. Conversely, Carolina's offense is top-five in the NFL in those same categories, and it looks like they'll get No. 2 wideout Jalen Coker back for this one. I like the Panthers to roll into Lincoln Financial Field and turn the heat up under Nick Sirianni's seat to a fever pitch. Projected score: Panthers 23, Eagles 21 The pick: Panthers +1.5 Pittsburgh Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers This is another game that has some outliers worth targeting. The Bucs will be at home after an upset win over the Cowboys last Thursday night in Dallas. They'll have the rest advantage over a Steelers team that took care of business against the Colts on Sunday. Similar to how I think the Cowboys sort of overlooked the then-winless Buccaneers with an undrafted rookie quarterback under center, Pittsburgh could get caught sleeping here, too. Not so much because they're going to overlook Jalon Daniels , but the Steelers could get caught looking ahead to their Week 7 matchup against the Saints in Paris. With a France trip on the horizon for Pittsburgh, I think Tampa Bay is a live home dog. Moreover, I think the Bucs defense has a good shot at containing the Steelers offense. Tampa Bay is allowing the second-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL through Week 5, which could limit Jaylen Warren's impact. Meanwhile, Todd Bowles has some solid splits against Aaron Rodgers over the course of his career as both a head coach and defensive coordinator. Rodgers' teams are 1-2 against Bowles and average just 16.7 points per game. Projected score: Buccaneers 24, Steelers 23 The pick: Buccaneers +3 Tennessee Titans at Indianapolis Colts Sunday, 1 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) You'll undoubtedly scratch your head at this pick, and it's hard to blame you. Tennessee hasn't instilled any confidence this season and is punting on a league-high 53% of its drives. Still, I think this line is too big in a divisional matchup against the Colts, whom I don't believe are a serious player in the AFC. The Indy offense can't move the ball efficiently, ranking 29th in the NFL in yards per play (4.6). Meanwhile, their defense is 28th in the league in total yards allowed (384.2). Daniel Jones has also turned the ball over more times (7) than he's found the end zone (4) this season. So, for as bad as the Titans offense has been this season, Indy isn't that far off, so I'll gladly put the full touchdown in my back pocket. Projected score: Colts 24, Titans 20 The pick: Titans +7 Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. (Fox, Stream: Fubo , try for free) I think we're firmly on backdoor alert with this line. L.A. is coming off an overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night, so this is quite the turnaround for Sean McVay's club. Matthew Stafford dropped back and threw 54 times in the loss, while the Rams offense ran 78 total plays. That could see them a bit sluggish in this contest. I don't envision Arizona pulling off the upset, but I do think they're capable of scoring late to get us within the number here. For instance, Arizona kept the offense on the field throughout a blowout loss to Detroit and scored a largely meaningless touchdown just before the two-minute warning. That's the type of play we'll be looking for them here. Projected score: Rams 30, Cardinals 17 The pick: Cardinals +13.5 New York Jets at New England Patriots I think the Patriots are all the way back. Drake Maye has seemingly returned to his MVP form from last year and just tallied five touchdowns in a blowout win over the Raiders . Gillette Stadium has been a comfortable spot for New England as they're 10-1 in their last 11 home games. Meanwhile, they've also taken care of business against inferior opponents under Mike Vrabel as the Patriots are 11-0 with him at the helm when facing teams entering with a losing record. Further looking at the trends for this one, the Patriots are 12-0 straight-up and 10-2 ATS in their last 12 games as a favorite and have a +17.9 PPG differential over that stretch. As for the Jets , they've yet to win or cover (0-6) a divisional game under head coach Aaron Glenn. And few teams are more disappointing thus far than the Philadelphia Eagles . Might Nick Sirianni get a pink slip if his club loses at home Sunday against a rested and surging Carolina Panthers team? High 58F. Winds NW at 5 to 10 mph. With the Eagles -1.5 at DraftKings , 94% of ATS handle is on them but 55% of bets are on the Panthers. There's heavy action on the Over with a low total of 40.5. The latest odds I saw post-Week 5 on the first NFL head coach fired had Washington's Dan Quinn as the +200 favorite and Sirianni next at +400. And that's absolutely no surprise to me after both NFC East head coaches made utterly stupid decisions that cost their teams victories this past Sunday. I'm sure you know by know what happened in Commanders-Giants and Eagles-Jaguars. Quinn and/or Jayden Daniels didn't even get a field-goal try off at end of overtime, with a win in Washington's hands. Maybe that clock mistake was on Daniels, but there's no doubt it's on Sirianni for having Jake Elliott kick off into the Jacksonville landing zone on Sunday in London. That allowed a long return and a walk-off 57-yard field goal to win. All the Eagles had to do was kick the ball out of the end zone and the Jags are at their 35 hoping for a Hail Mary with no timeouts. Kudos to Sirianni for taking the blame, but he wouldn't take any for managing the prior scoring drive in a way that left the Jaguars with more time than they should have had. Two passes stopped the clock, and Elliott kicked the go-ahead field goal with 12 seconds left. Why not run it down to only a couple and make that the final play? "I'm honoring a play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," QB Jalen Hurts said afterward. "We're not asking him to make play calls in that scenario," Sirianni responded to Monday. Starting to feel a disconnect there? The Eagles' next game is on a bit of extra rest, as it is Monday night in Week 7 vs. Dallas, so you might see a change if this goes badly Sunday, even though Sirianni is 67-33 as the Eagles head coach. That's tied for the fifth-best head coaching record through 100 games in the league since 1970. The team's bye isn't until Week 10, and you can already hear the Mike Tomlin rumors. This marks Sirianni's third three-game losing streak in Philadelphia, and he has never lost four in a row. It's not just his clock management, but his offense has been lousy during this skid in averaging 14.7 points and 217 yards per game while converting just 22.2% of third downs. The PPG is the fewest for Philly through five games since 2012, and the YPG the fewest through five since 1999. A juggled offensive line hasn't helped. With Lane Johnson having retired, Cam Jurgens traded and Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, the team has replaced three starters already. And it's not clear yet if the offense will have tailback and former NFL Offensive Player of the Year Saquon Barkley and No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith back from injury yet, after both missed Week 5. The Eagles are averaging a scant 3.5 yards per play with both off the field this season, compared to 5.3 in all other situations. It's possible the Eagles are down to their No. 4 tailback because No. 2 Tank Bigsby is on IR and No. 3 Will Shipley was hurt against the Jags. This will mark the first time the Eagles will take the field sitting below .500 since 2021, when they were 6-7. The 76 straight games played without a losing record was the longest streak in team history. The overall NFL record is 145 by the Patriots from 2003-12. Carolina comes off its bye with its 2-2 mark the team's best four-game start since 2021. It's also good enough for the lead in the ultra-weak NFC South – the Panthers are +130 favorites. We get a former all-Alabama quarterback matchup here in Bryce Young vs. Hurts with Young off to his best start and perhaps answering all those lingering questions that have dogged the former No. 1 overall pick. Thanks to Young and sensational second-year wideout Tetairoa McMillan , the Panthers rank top five in the league in scoring offense (30.3 PPG), total offense (405.8 YPG) and passing offense (301.3 YPG). The scoring average is the best in franchise history through four games, and it's their first time averaging at least 30.0 PPG in any four-game span since 2019. Young would make history if he keeps his NFL-best 317.0-yard passing average up, as no QB ever has averaged even 275 yards passing in a season after three straight years under 200.0 passing yards per. Young also led the NFL entering his bye week with 11 completions on deep throws (20+ air yards). He is 0-1 against Hurts in the NFL as the Eagles beat the visiting Panthers 22-16 in the most recent meeting in December 2024. momentum as they take on the Philadelphia Eagles (2-3). Carolina enters Week 6 in first place in the NFC South, one half game ahead of the Falcons (2-3). The Panthers boast one of the league’s most productive offenses, averaging just over 30 points per game behind a breakout season from quarterback Bryce Young . Losers of three in a row, a banged-up Philadelphia is reeling a bit following a brutal loss in London this past weekend, 19-17 to Jacksonville. Prior to their bye, the Panthers outlasted the Bears in Charlotte, 32-26. The aforementioned Young threw for 329 yards and a couple touchdowns, Tetairoa McMillan caught 14 balls for 192 yards including both Young touchdown passes and Chuba Hubbard ran for 122 yards and two scores in the win. Bryce Young has now thrown for 1268 yards including nine touchdowns and just two interceptions through four games this season. Philadelphia’s most recent outing was a head-scratcher. With a patchwork offensive line and numerous skill position players sidelined, the Eagles somehow managed to take a lead over Jacksonville in London, 17-16 with eight seconds to play in the fourth quarter. The Eagles elected not to kick off through the endzone…as well as tackle kick returner Ameer Abdullah until he had rambled 53 yards to the Philly 39-yard line with one second to play. Cam Little then came on to drill a game-winning 57-yard field goal as the Eagles snatched defeat from the jaws of victory. Prior to the mayhem in the final moments, Jalen Hurts threw for 220 yards and a touchdown to Darius Cooper . Minus the injured Saquon Barkley , the Eagles rushed for a paltry 22 yards in the game. While Philadelphia’s long list of injuries tops this game’s storylines, the play under center for each team will be noteworthy. Bryce Young appears to be taking a major step forward in his third NFL season as the Panthers’ offense is currently one of the league’s most explosive. Jalen Hurts has been either really good this season (two games) or subpar (three games). It is no coincidence that the poor performances have coincided with the Birds’ three-game losing streak. A third storyline to pay attention to is the turnover battle. Carolina enters the week with a +3 turnover differential while Philadelphia has coughed the ball up two more times than it has taken the ball away. The Eagles have dominated this series winning 11 of the 13 all-time meetings including each of the last five. Their most recent meeting came on December 8, 2024, when Philadelphia escaped with a 22-16 victory. In the past, Sunday would be a get right spot for Philly, but Carolina takes the field with a substantial rest advantage and playing better football. There is something to be said however, about a desperate football team and the Eagles should be desperate come the weekend. away.headline: NFL analyst picks Panthers over Eagles for Week 6 matchup
away.blurb: Besides being out of running backs, the other problem for the Eagles is that they've struggled to stop the pass this year and they're facing a Panthers team that is SECOND in the NFL in passing yards per game. I never thought in my entire life that I'd type out anything like that about Carolina's offense, but here we are. The deck is stacked against the Eagles, so I have no choice here; I'm taking the Panthers. PICK: Panthers (+1.5) 27-24 over Eagles However, the Eagles are far from healthy going into Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Their offensive line is battered by injuries, their right tackle Lane Johnson just suddenly retired and they're down to their practice-squad running backs. Carolina has plenty of injury issues of their own , but at least one analyst thinks they can pull off a win this week. John Breech at CBS Sports is predicting a victory for the Panthers: It's not a wild take given the situation. In fact, they were one Xavier Legette drop away from upsetting the Eagles the last time they visited Philly two years ago. Plus, the Eagles' struggling offense may not be able to take advantage of what might be the Panthers' biggest weakness—their banged-up cornerback room. Even without starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, Carolina might not have too difficult of a time keeping down the league's fifth-worst passing attack—especially if it's still missing their top wideout in DeVonta Smith. away.headline: Eagles' RB crisis collides with Panthers' vulnerable run defense
away.blurb: Saquon Barkley remained sidelined Wednesday, listed as a nonparticipant because of the hamstring injury that kept him out against Jacksonville. Will Shipley was also listed as a nonparticipant with a foot injury after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported a partial tear of his plantar fascia and that he could miss multiple weeks. With Tank Bigsby on injured reserve, Philadelphia’s depth has become a pressing concern. The matchup offers an opening. Carolina has allowed 626 rushing yards in four games, averaging 156.5 per game and 5.4 per carry. Those numbers give offensive coordinator Sean Mannion a reason to keep working toward a functional rushing attack, even if Barkley remains unavailable. Pierce would be positioned for a larger workload if Barkley cannot play. He carried 11 times for 14 yards against Jacksonville, part of a team performance that produced just 22 rushing yards on 18 attempts in the 19-17 loss. That leaves the Eagles evaluating how to divide carries, handle passing-down responsibilities, and potentially use Steele to help create room for another runner. Pierce and Steele are available options, but the coaching staff has not announced a workload split. Barkley’s return would change that calculation, though Wednesday’s absence left his availability unresolved. Until he participates more, Philadelphia needs a workable plan built around the backs who are practicing. Depending on what happens at practice over the next two days, the Eagles could be down to Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele at running back Sunday, but Carolina’s struggling run defense gives Philadelphia an opportunity to repair a ground game that stalled in London. Steele represents another option, although an offensive role would be a change from London. He got all 20 of his snaps against Jacksonville on special teams. Mannion said Tuesday that the team was considering using Steele as a lead blocker, praising his versatility without confirming a specific role. The blocking must improve alongside the rotation. Carolina’s season averages offer encouragement, but the Eagles still need to execute well enough to turn a favorable matchup into productive early-down carries. After three straight losses and three straight NFC East games, Philadelphia needs its rushing attack to sustain possessions and ease the burden on Jalen Hurts. Sunday’s opponent offers a chance for a depleted backfield to help with that reset. This article originally appeared on Eagles Wire: Eagles' RB crisis collides with Panthers' vulnerable run defense

Greenard didn't practice at all last week, but was questionable and a game-time decision before ultimately not being able to play. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported this week that the Panthers are 'hopeful' that Coker can return in Week 6 when the Panthers travel to Philadelphia to face the Eagles. In the report, Fowler mentioned that Young is using the RPO as a weapon in the offense with the Detroit game perfectly showcasing that. Coker may not be the only player on offense to return after the Week 5 bye, either. Head coach Dave Canales told reporters after the Week 4 win that running back Trevor Etienne will for sure be back. Carolina has been without Jonathon Brooks who suffered an injury in the Week 2 win over the Atlanta Falcons. Chuba Hubbard and AJ Dillon have handled the work load so far with Brooks out but getting another back in the lineup can beneficial for the Panthers. The Panthers return to action in Week 6 as they travel to Philadelphia to face the Eagles. At 2-2, the Panthers are tied on top of the NFC South with the Atlanta Falcons but do have the tiebreaker due to a win in Week 2. Carolina's passing offense has been one of the best in the NFL through the first four weeks and they are hoping to keep that going. They took advantage of a bad Lions defense, putting up big numbers. That effort was led by quarterback Bryce Young and wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan. With the offense clicking, the Panthers could be the favorite to win the NFC South this season for the second straight year. They are also doing all of this with some key injuries to both offense and defense. Among the players injured on offense is wide receiver Jalen Coker who got hurt in the Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns. Adding in Coker should make this offense much better. Through the first four weeks of the season, Coker has 18 receptions for 222 yards and two touchdowns in three games. He was the leading receiver going into Week 4 before Tetairoa McMillan had a career day in the win over the Lions. Now, as the season goes on, the thoughts of having Coker and McMillan playing at a high level in this offense is very intriguing.

home.headline: Jalen Hurts dealing with 'very unique' injury as Philadelphia Eagles QB adds to mystery
home.blurb: He was never downgraded to questionable or doubtful and had no injury designation for the game but remains on the latest injury report as a full participant with a calf injury this week. Hurts is far from the biggest concern for the Eagles and their injury situation, though head coach Nick Sirianni said he is 'hopeful' Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith will return this weekend against the Carolina Panthers. Before Sunday's Jaguars loss, Hurts said: ' This is when you find out what you have. You find out who you're going out there to battle with. 'You see how you respond to adversity, how you show up to work every day, what's your energy, what's your level of persistence and resilience and determination to go out there and do the job.' Jalen Hurts is among 24 Philadelphia Eagles players currently listed on their lengthy injury report. And he added more mystery to the situation surrounding his condition when quizzed on Wednesday as he shared he has a 'very unique' injury. Hurts was listed as a full participant with a calf injury last Friday, two days before losing to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. And while there is no indication he will miss time, Hurts did little to shed light on the extent or nature of his discomfort when speaking to the media in his midweek press conference. 'It was a very unique experience, to say the least,' Hurts said. 'I don't want to get into the details of kind of leading up to the game and whatnot, but got nicked up in the Rams game.' His comments raised more questions than answers, particularly given he was not added to the injury report until nearly a week after the Rams game where he said he 'got nicked up.' Discussing their injury crisis earlier this month, Sirianni said: 'This is life in the NFL, and we will do the things that we can control to put ourselves in the best position to win against a very good football team. 'You will never hear me use anything as an excuse. Our job is to go handle the things that we can control, tough, detailed and together, and put ourselves in the best position to win this upcoming week.' Hurts, meanwhile, knows he is in a situation where he has a lot to prove with his supporting cast severely depleted.

The Eagles didn’t list the QB on their injury report until last Friday, just before boarding a plane to London. home.headline: NFL analyst picks Panthers over Eagles for Week 6 matchup
home.blurb: Besides being out of running backs, the other problem for the Eagles is that they've struggled to stop the pass this year and they're facing a Panthers team that is SECOND in the NFL in passing yards per game. I never thought in my entire life that I'd type out anything like that about Carolina's offense, but here we are. The deck is stacked against the Eagles, so I have no choice here; I'm taking the Panthers. PICK: Panthers (+1.5) 27-24 over Eagles However, the Eagles are far from healthy going into Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Their offensive line is battered by injuries, their right tackle Lane Johnson just suddenly retired and they're down to their practice-squad running backs. Carolina has plenty of injury issues of their own , but at least one analyst thinks they can pull off a win this week. John Breech at CBS Sports is predicting a victory for the Panthers: It's not a wild take given the situation. In fact, they were one Xavier Legette drop away from upsetting the Eagles the last time they visited Philly two years ago. Plus, the Eagles' struggling offense may not be able to take advantage of what might be the Panthers' biggest weakness—their banged-up cornerback room. Even without starters Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson, Carolina might not have too difficult of a time keeping down the league's fifth-worst passing attack—especially if it's still missing their top wideout in DeVonta Smith. home.headline: Eagles' RB crisis collides with Panthers' vulnerable run defense
home.blurb: Saquon Barkley remained sidelined Wednesday, listed as a nonparticipant because of the hamstring injury that kept him out against Jacksonville. Will Shipley was also listed as a nonparticipant with a foot injury after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported a partial tear of his plantar fascia and that he could miss multiple weeks. With Tank Bigsby on injured reserve, Philadelphia’s depth has become a pressing concern. The matchup offers an opening. Carolina has allowed 626 rushing yards in four games, averaging 156.5 per game and 5.4 per carry. Those numbers give offensive coordinator Sean Mannion a reason to keep working toward a functional rushing attack, even if Barkley remains unavailable. Pierce would be positioned for a larger workload if Barkley cannot play. He carried 11 times for 14 yards against Jacksonville, part of a team performance that produced just 22 rushing yards on 18 attempts in the 19-17 loss. That leaves the Eagles evaluating how to divide carries, handle passing-down responsibilities, and potentially use Steele to help create room for another runner. Pierce and Steele are available options, but the coaching staff has not announced a workload split. Barkley’s return would change that calculation, though Wednesday’s absence left his availability unresolved. Until he participates more, Philadelphia needs a workable plan built around the backs who are practicing. Depending on what happens at practice over the next two days, the Eagles could be down to Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele at running back Sunday, but Carolina’s struggling run defense gives Philadelphia an opportunity to repair a ground game that stalled in London. Steele represents another option, although an offensive role would be a change from London. He got all 20 of his snaps against Jacksonville on special teams. Mannion said Tuesday that the team was considering using Steele as a lead blocker, praising his versatility without confirming a specific role. The blocking must improve alongside the rotation. Carolina’s season averages offer encouragement, but the Eagles still need to execute well enough to turn a favorable matchup into productive early-down carries. After three straight losses and three straight NFC East games, Philadelphia needs its rushing attack to sustain possessions and ease the burden on Jalen Hurts. Sunday’s opponent offers a chance for a depleted backfield to help with that reset. This article originally appeared on Eagles Wire: Eagles' RB crisis collides with Panthers' vulnerable run defense

picks.headline: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Week 6 Tracker: Injury updates, predictions, storylines and more
picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Buccaneers Week 6 Tracker: Injury updates, predictions, storylines and more - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Pittsburgh Steelers RB Jaylen Warren (L) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers edge rusher Rueben Bain Jr. (R) | Lauren Leigh Bacho and Perry Knotts - Getty Images | Graphic by Adam Patrick Shayne Kubas Wed, October 14, 2026 at 10:00 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Coming off their thrilling 34-22 home victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5, the 3-2 Pittsburgh Steelers head south this week to face the 1-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who themselves are coming off their first win of the season last week against the Dallas Cowboys. Despite their record (and an injury to starting quarterback Baker Mayfield), the Bucs are coming off their two most competitive games of the season, with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels filling in for Mayfield. It looks as though Daniels will once again be the one under center against Pittsburgh, and they can't allow him to look nearly as comfortable as Dallas did a week ago. Tampa Bay and Pittsburgh haven't played each other many times, but the Steelers have dominated those meetings 10-2. To keep pace in a hotly contested AFC North, they badly need that to become 11-2 this weekend. Everything you could want to know about this matchup, including injury updates, weather forecasts, storylines, and more, can be found right here. So make sure to bookmark this page and come back throughout the week. How to Watch Pittsburgh Steelers vs Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6 Date: Sunday, October 18 Time: 1:00 p.m. EST TV Network: CBS Announcers: Andrew Catalon (Play-by-Play), Logan Ryan (Color Analyst), AJ Ross (Sideline Reporter) Pittsburgh Steelers Injury Report for Week 6 Steelers injury reports will be available here once they are released, beginning Wednesday, October 14 Tampa Bay Buccaneers Injury Report for Week 6 Buccaneers injury reports will be available here once they are released, beginning Wednesday, October 14 Weather Forecast for Pittsburgh Steelers vs Tampa Buccaneers Week 6 Current Forecast ( via NFLWeather.com ) Temperature: 79 degrees Wind Speed: 20 mph Precipitation: Isolated Rain Showers Biggest Pittsburgh Steelers Storylines heading into Week 6 Can Jaylen Warren keep up his unbelievable run against a tough Tampa run defense? Calling what Jaylen Warren has done over the past three games "unbelievable may not be the right word, since many Steelers fans have seen glimpses of the level of play he's reached this season. Still, three consecutive games with over 125 yards from scrimmage is no small feat. In fact, Warren is the only player to do that so far this season. The Buccaneers will be his toughest test so far by a mile; however, they are allowing just 3.28 yards per attempt on the ground, according to Sumer Sports . If Warren can maintain his level of production against a tough opponent like Tampa Bay, then his breakout will feel even more real than it already does. Can the Steelers' run defense shut down another high-powered run game? No Derrick Harmon, no problem for the Steelers in Week 5 against the Colts' rushing attack. Despite facing star running back Jonathan Taylor, Pittsburgh completely shut down the run against Indianapolis. They allowed just 66 yards on 24 attempts for a measly 2.8 yards per carry. While Harmon's absence didn't hurt them last week, the Buccaneers' run game has actually been more efficient than the Colts' this year, even before the Steelers crushed them a week ago. Bucky Irving looks much more like the player who burst onto the scene as a rookie in 2024, increasing his yards-per-attempt average from 3.4 last season to 5.3 so far this year. If Pittsburgh can slow him down with Harmon still on Injured Reserve, it should give the unit a ton of confidence moving forward. Will Tampa Bay play more man coverage, and can the Steelers handle it if they do? The Steelers' offense looks much better over the past three games after struggling mightily to start the season, but their kryptonite has remained the same for most of their five games: man coverage. Pittsburgh's receivers simply aren't winning often enough when teams man them up, and Aaron Rodgers' unwillingness to stay calm in the pocket isn't exactly helping either. The old gunslinger can still carve up zone for the most part, but unless his receivers can win almost immediately against man, he simply doesn't have the same playmaking ability he once had. Tampa Bay has played man on just 19.1% of their snaps this season, according to Sumer Sports. Will that change against Pittsburgh? And if it does, can they find success despite being down three receivers? Speaking of... Will the Steelers' offense change at all with multiple receivers now on the shelf? Pittsburgh will head into Week 6 down three receivers : Roman Wilson, Michael Pittman Jr., and special teams ace Ben Skowronek. For a team that wants to live in 11 personnel and in the shotgun, it could mean a serious change in how they operate until at least one of them returns. Pittsburgh shifted to more 12 and 22 personnel in the second half of Week 5 once Wilson and Skowronek went down, but will that plan carry over into next week? It's hard to say for sure given how Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy prefer to run the offense, but I certainly hope they are smart enough to lean on their tight ends and running backs without their full group of playmakers available. Even when everyone has been healthy, they have been far more effective when using heavier formations, so the offense may actually be in a better situation despite the unfortunate injuries. picks.blurb: Opening lines: Spread: Buccaneers -1.5 Moneyline: Buccaneers -125; Steelers +105 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Buccaneers vs Steelers expert picks Adam Kaufman: Steelers 23, Buccaneers 17 Tampa Bay finally got its win, and Bucky Irving deserves plenty of the credit. Running all over Dallas is one thing. Repeating that against Pittsburgh is a tougher assignment. For now, I'm working under the assumption Jalon Daniels gets another start. He handled himself well Thursday, but the Steelers should make the rookie work harder for his completions and give him fewer comfortable situations. Aaron Rodgers doesn't need to turn this into a track meet. Take the available throws, avoid the costly mistake and make the Buccaneers drive the field. No easy task down Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr., but Germie Bernard is emerging and Jaylen Warren is a one-man wrecking crew. The Bucs' extra rest keeps this interesting. I still like the Steelers' defense to produce the decisive stop — or takeaway — in a game where points require some effort. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Steelers 20, Buccaneers 16 With frustrations growing, both Tampa Bay and Pittsburgh got their houses in better order last week. Which team can continue the effort on Sunday? The Steelers could get another big all-purpose outing from Jaylen Warren, and Aaron Rodgers is unlikely to be bothered by a pass rush that hasn't generated much heat. Unless things break right for him, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels could have a hard time feeling at home in his third start. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Buccaneers 23, Steelers 20 The Jalon Daniels Bucs are a frisky bunch. Everyone (rightfully) wrote off Tampa after starting 0-4, especially when it became clear that Baker Mayfield wouldn't be walking through that door anytime soon. Then Daniels and Co. marched into Dallas to steal a win on Thursday Night Football. Now the season has been saved, especially in an NFC South race that remains wide open. This week, the Bucs welcome the wounded Steelers to town. Considering Pittsburgh's receivers are dropping like flies, Tampa has a good chance to pull off another upset. away.headline: Could Antoine Winfield Jr. return in Week 6 game vs. Steelers?
away.blurb: Winfield suffered a rib injury and was forced to miss Tampa Bay's Week 5 victory over the Dallas Cowboys. Head coach Todd Bowles said Winfield could be out two to four weeks after suffering the setback. As expected, the veteran safety was once again unable to practice on Wednesday ahead of the Buccaneers' game against Pittsburgh and should be viewed as doubtful to play in Week 6. This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: Could Antoine Winfield Jr. return in Week 6 game vs. Steelers? The Pittsburgh Steelers ' Week 6 opponents, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , saw one of their defensive stars miss practice ahead of Sunday's matchup. Courtesy of the initial Week 6 practice report, the Buccaneers saw standout safety Antoine Winfield Jr. miss Wednesday's session with a rib injury. The Steelers also saw a few defensive starters miss practice, but a few were non-injury-related. Drafted by the Buccaneers in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft, Winfield has appeared in 89 games, recording 534 tackles, 18 sacks, nine interceptions, and 12 forced fumbles. Winfield also earned First-Team All-Pro recognition in 2023. With Winfield expected to miss, Ifeatu Melifonwu will serve as the starting safety opposite Tykee Smith. Pittsburgh's now high-powered offense should, in theory, find tremendous success against this injury-ridden Tampa Bay secondary. away.headline: Steelers injury report: Pittsburgh enters road trip with abundance of injuries
away.blurb: Out of the bye, road trips to face the division rival Bengals and in-state rival Eagles await. Neither is a long trip in terms of mileage, but the Steelers have not won in Philadelphia since 1965, and it follows an AFC North dogfight. The receivers room is the most pressing problem. Pittman will be out for at least the next three games after being placed on injured reserve. The veteran was a key offseason acquisition but has only played in three games in which he’s caught seven passes for 89 yards. The extent of the injuries to Wilson and Skowronek, sustained against Indianapolis, are not yet known, but McCarthy said Monday that both will be out for at least the Tampa Bay game. The secondary is a bit better off. Ramsey spent the week leading up to the Colts game on the injury report but handled a normal workload. Only Dean was absent, and the Steelers have not yet taken the step of adding the free agent cornerback signing to injured reserve. Dean was a limited practice participant Wednesday while Ramsey was out with a wrist injury listed. McCarthy hinted strongly that Dowdle is expected back this week from the toe injury he sustained in Week 2 against New England. He was also limited Wednesday. That should help the offense manage the reps of Jaylen Warren, who’s handled a heavy workload in Dowdle’s absence. First-year coach Mike McCarthy’s team will play four of its next five games on the road starting this week, and it will take multiple longer – and daunting – trips to do so before things begin to moderate in the back half of the 2026 schedule. All of it will unfold amid mounting absences. Running back Rico Dowdle; receivers Michael Pittman Jr., Roman Wilson and Ben Skowronek; and defensive backs Jamel Dean and Jalen Ramsey have all been hurt in some form or fashion recently. The stretch will be one of, if not the, most grueling in the franchise’s history and could determine whether the Steelers ’ 3-2 start has legs, or whether another mediocre year awaits a franchise that hasn’t won an NFL playoff game since 2017. NFL Week 6 brings a road trip to Tampa Bay to face the Buccaneers . That’s a 1,000-or-so-mile trip right off the bat against a desperate 1-4 team that needs a win to preserve any postseason hopes. One week later, the Steelers will board a long flight to Paris to face the New Orleans Saints in the first NFL regular season game in France. It will be only the second international game for Pittsburgh since 2013. It picked up a win against Minnesota in Dublin, Ireland last October, but the travel schedule was much kinder surrounding that date. The Steelers got to enjoy a bye after their trip to the Emerald Isle and did not need to travel any further than Massachusetts until they visited the Los Angeles Chargers in early November. It was a similar story when they played in London13 years ago. They came home to a bye, and most travel was relatively local for the month before and after. away.headline: Steelers Injury Central: Two More WRs Ruled Out This Week
away.blurb: Steelers Injury Central: Two More WRs Ruled Out This Week Opens in a new tab Steelers News Two Pittsburgh Steelers, wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back next week, either. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, did not play on Sunday after being listed as questionable. Ben Skowronek has been ruled out of the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday, Oct. 12. Skowronek was injured in the second quarter, was treated in the sideline medical tent, and then went straight to the locker room. He did not return to the sideline in the second half. Wide receiver Roman Wilson has been ruled out of the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, head coach Mike McCarthy said on Monday, Oct. 12. Michael Pittman Jr. is expected to miss multiple weeks, after suffered a setback in his left foot injury. He has been ruled out for the Week 5 game against the Indianapolis Colts. Pittman seen with his injured foot on a scooter after practice on Wednesday, Oct. 7, and was listed as a limited participant in the session. He did not practice on Thursday, Oct. 8 or Friday, Oct. 9. Pittman played against the Cleveland Browns in Week 4 and had been a full participant in the team's practices leading up to that game. Pittman dressed and started after being listed as questionable to play against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3. Pittman was downgraded to out for Week 2 after the team's final practice of Week 2 on Saturday, Sept. 19. Pittman did not practice on Thursday or Friday after first being limited in practice with an injury on Wednesday, Sept. 17. Defensive back Jalen Ramsey is questionable to play against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 6 after he was limited in practice on Thursday, Oct. 8 and Friday, Oct. 9 and did not practice on Wednesday, Oct. 7. It's unclear if Ramsey suffered a setback with regards to his fractured right wrist, or if the team is simply managing his reps as he plays through the pain of the injury. Ramsey played in Week 4 after being listed as questionable and being limited in all three of the team's practices. He had his arm in a sling for Monday's practice, but ditched the sling for a cast on Tuesday. Brandin Echols will likely replace Ramsey if he can't return to action. Running back Rico Dowdle was a limited participant in practice for the third straight day on Friday, Oct. 9, his first practice work since suffering a dislocated toe on his left foot in Week 2. He is officially questionable to play in Week 5. Dowdle did not play in the Steelers' Week 4 game against the Cleveland Browns

Indianapolis rules out four players, with no true surprises. That said, the Colts will be down two starters on defense. Defensive end Arden Key is expected to miss multiple games with his hamstring injury, with this week being the first. Linebacker Jaylon Carlies, who had an interception for the Colts last week, also suffered a rib injury that will keep him out of this Sunday's contest. Ashton Dulin will miss his third game of the season already, so the Colts will have to make things work on special teams without their top gunner. Tight end Will Mallory just had his 21-day practice window opened on Wednesday after starting the season on injured reserve, but him being ruled out against Pittsburgh proves the Colts are using an abundance of caution with him moving forward. Center Tanor Bortolini went from limited on Wednesday to a full participant Thursday, and now logged another full practice Friday. He enters the weekend without an injury designation and will start. That's an underrated development, as Indy's offensive line has been stellar through the first month and losing continuity would be a big hit to the unit's current positive momentum. There's three Colts listed as questionable this week, with two wide receivers. Keenan Allen is questionable for the second week in a row, but completed a full practice on Friday, which is a significant step towards suiting up this weekend. Darius Slayton is a new addition to the injury report late in the week having been limited on Friday with a knee injury. Given the issue appears to have just popped up, Slayton may have to wait yet another week to make his Colts debut. Cornerback Charvarius Ward is trending towards playing. After two straight days being limited, Ward was a full participant in the week's final session. The questionable tag does add a little uncertainty, but a week of progress indicates Ward should be good to go. Finally, it's worth noting that defensive tackle DeForest Buckner did not practice Friday due to rest. No reason to worry about the veteran, though, as he doesn't have any injury designation. Not as long a final list for the Steelers, but a top-heavy report. Worst case scenario, Pittsburgh could be without four starters. picks.blurb: Opening lines: Spread: Rams -13.5 Moneyline: Rams -750; Cardinals +13.5 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Rams vs Cardinals expert picks Adam Kaufman: Rams 34, Cardinals 20 The Rams need a get-right game. Conveniently, the Cardinals are coming to town. Los Angeles has spent enough time trading punches with contenders. Now Matthew Stafford gets an Arizona defense that should provide a much friendlier afternoon, even with the shortened turnaround after Monday night. The Cardinals can move the ball through Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, and Jeremiyah Love gives the offense a reason to stay patient. I just don't see enough defensive resistance to keep the Rams from eventually creating separation, especially after the way they fell to the Bills . The concern is asking Los Angeles to cover a huge number after an overtime game. Winning this matchup feels considerably more straightforward. Give me Stafford, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Kyren Williams and enough explosive plays to put the Rams back in the win column. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Rams 38, Cardinals 20 Watch out, Arizona. The Rams might take out the frustrations of a 2-3 start on their divisional foe. The Cardinals haven't proven nearly capable of offering any resistance to an attack with as much firepower as Los Angeles, let alone stopping one. Maybe this isn't the game in which Carson Beck will make his NFL debut for Arizona as he looks to take on a role as more than a mere emergency quarterback, but a blowout might bring that possibility closer to reality. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Rams 31, Cardinals 16 Perhaps the Rams aren't the super team that we thought. A 2-3 start to the season certainly isn't doing the team any favors. However, Matthew Stafford looked like a quarterback that started to find himself again in Week 5 against the Bills. The Cardinals are the get-right team for every NFC West team that feels down about themselves. That's just the reality of being the doormat in a loaded division. Sean McVay's crew takes out all their frustrations on the lowly Cardinals, winning by a big margin to cover up all the special teams mistakes. Live Simms Unbuttoned Rotoworld Bet Staff , Rotoworld Bet Staff It is not shocking that the Cardinals (1-4) have struggled to start the season, but it is a surprise that the Rams (2-3) are below .500 through five games. The 2026 campaign will get better for one of them as a result of their game this Sunday at SoFi Stadium. Under first-year Head Coach Mike LaFleur, the Cardinals take the field following a rough 45-21 home loss to the Detroit Lions. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett produced one of his better performances of the season, completing 29 of 47 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns. Tight end Trey McBride continued to be Brissett’s most reliable target with nine catches for 66 yards and a score. Arizona’s offense though was it was one-dimensional. They could not establish any semblance of a running game against the Lions. In addition, they were overwhelmed defensively by Detroit’s offense. Those woes on defense have been a consistent theme this season. Arizona has allowed 162 points through five games (32.4PPG). No team in the NFL has allowed more points than the Cards. The Rams own the NFL’s top-ranked offense in yards per game at 424.4. The numbers make this week’s game against Arizona look like a get right spot for the preseason favorites to win the Super Bowl. As noted, Sean McVay’s club has moved the ball consistently, but they have had issues turning long drives into points. They have scored a pedestrian 119 points this season through five games. The biggest storylines Sunday thus center on whether Arizona’s defense can slow Stafford and whether the Rams can turn yards gained into points. For the Rams, this game feels close to a must-win if they want to remain within striking distance of first-place San Francisco in the NFC West. Defensive lineman Walter Nolen III and rookie linebacker Karson Sharar were added to the report with injuries that happened during practice Wednesday or during Thursday's workout. Nolen missed the first seven games of his rookie season last year with a calf injury, so that is something to watch. away.blurb: TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up. Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams Skip to main content SI.COM "Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday. Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered. There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles. "Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said. "And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday." Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air. Donald had been dealing with a back injury, while Parkinson missed Week 4 with shoulder and knee injuries. Watson dislocated his shoulder in Week 3 and missed the following week but he's back for L.A. The Rams and Bills square off on Monday night at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. home.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams are set to enter Week 6 the healthiest they’ve been in weeks ahead of their matchup against the Arizona Cardinals. While the Rams didn't practice on Wednesday, each player's status is an estimation. On the injury report Rams had only one player who was estimated to not participate. That player was tight end Davis Allen, who would have missed practice with a foot injury. Outside of Allen, the Rams only had five other players listed, with four of them limited. While Allen is the only player who was estimated as a non-participant, linebacker Nate Landman (wrist/shoulder), wide receiver Alex Bachman (wrist), tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder), and cornerback Josh Wallace (shoulder) were all limited. Both Landman and Parkinson have been on the injury report over the last few weeks as they manage various injuries. The Rams have managed Landman during the week before the last few games and will likely do the same with Parkinson. Jeremiyah Love's (2nd) ankle injury will keep him out of practice Wednesday and there is a chance he doesn't play against Rams. "The rest for him will be vital." Arizona had multiple players who did not practice Wednesday due to rest. However, safety Wydett Williams didn’t participate as he goes through the concussion protocol. Additionally, safety Kitan Crawford and wide receiver Devin Duvernay were both limited. There are still a few situations to monitor throughout the week on the Rams’ side, particularly at tight end with Allen and Parkinson. However, compared to where things stood over the previous few weeks, they are in a much better position from a health standpoint. With the Rams looking to get back to .500 against the Cardinals, having most of their key contributors available should give them every opportunity to do just that. Kansas City is 4-0 after its bye, while Los Angeles is 0-5 following a 23-17 loss to Denver. Kickoff at Arrowhead Stadium is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. The Chiefs are favored by 8.5 points, but a routine favorite winning comfortably would hardly qualify as a bold prediction. Instead, this forecast projects an exceptional rushing performance, an unexpected Chargers defensive highlight and a fourth-quarter rally that changes the complexion of the afternoon without changing the winner. Kenneth Walker III rushes for 200 yards and three touchdowns Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Walker has already accumulated 537 rushing yards and four touchdowns on 87 carries through four games. That translates to more than six yards per attempt, giving Kansas City a foundation for dominating without asking Patrick Mahomes to carry every possession. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Chiefs average 6.5 yards per offensive play compared with the Chargers' 4.8. Their third-down conversion rate is also substantially better: 44% against 34.85%. Those advantages can sustain drives and produce the repeated rushing opportunities necessary for a monster individual afternoon. The prediction goes beyond another efficient outing. Walker reaches 200 rushing yards for the game and scores three times, becoming the central reason Kansas City controls possession and repeatedly finishes drives. There is an important limitation: Los Angeles allows only 5.0 yards per play, the same figure as Kansas City. This is not a forecast built on pretending the Chargers cannot defend. It depends on Walker maintaining his explosiveness while the Chiefs create an unusually favorable game script. If Kansas City builds an early advantage, sustained rushing volume can turn Walker's strong start into the biggest performance of his season. The Chargers intercept Patrick Mahomes twice, including a pick-six Mahomes has thrown nine touchdown passes against two interceptions through four games, with a 106.2 passer rating. Predicting two interceptions in one afternoon means Los Angeles matches his entire season total, despite entering winless. The statistical route to that surprise exists. The Chargers allow opponents to convert just 31.25% of third downs, compared with Kansas City's 37.04%. Forcing longer, obvious passing situations could provide opportunities that disappear when Walker keeps the offense ahead of schedule. Los Angeles needs more than ordinary defensive stops because its offense averages just 16.8 points per game. A defensive touchdown would change both field position and scoreboard pressure without requiring Justin Herbert to repeatedly rescue stalled possessions. The call is that one aggressive coverage read becomes an interception return for a touchdown, while another takeaway interrupts a promising Chiefs drive. That would be an unexpected blemish on Mahomes' efficient opening month. It would also illustrate why a team's record does not eliminate its capacity to produce a game-changing individual moment. Justin Herbert leads a 17-point fourth quarter, but Kansas City survives Herbert's current numbers make this the most counterintuitive offensive prediction: 937 passing yards, five touchdowns, seven interceptions and a 70.2 passer rating through five games. He has also absorbed 17 sacks. Against Denver, he managed 121 passing yards and was sacked five times. Receiving availability remains uncertain after Ladd McConkey dressed without playing, Quentin Johnston missed the game and Tre' Harris suffered a hamstring injury. Nevertheless, the prediction is that Herbert finally finds rhythm against a defense protecting a substantial lead. Two touchdown drives and a field goal produce 17 fourth-quarter points, forcing Kansas City to finish the game with its offense rather than coast. Walker provides that answer. The final forecast is Chiefs 38, Chargers 31: Kansas City remains unbeaten, but Los Angeles delivers a much stronger response than its record suggests. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Kansas City, but divisional familiarity and turnovers can make a comfortable matchup unpredictable. (AP) — Los Angeles Chargers tackle Rashawn Slater was placed on injured reserve Friday after having right ankle surgery. Slater had the surgery Thursday after a high ankle sprain in last weekend's loss to the Seattle Seahawks . He'll miss at least four games. The team said Slater will begin rehab immediately. Slater missed all of last season after rupturing the patellar tendon in his left knee in training camp. He signed a $114 million, four-year extension in July 2025. Slater is the latest in a string of injuries for the Chargers (0-4), who host Denver on Sunday. home.headline: Chiefs’ WR injury woes could be fixed with one major trade
home.blurb: Knox recently named the Chiefs as a possible landing spot for disgruntled Cleveland Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy, suggesting the Chiefs could send the Browns a conditional 2027 fifth-round pick in return. “According to NFL insider Jordan Schultz, it’s ‘pretty well known around the league’ that Jeudy is available,” Knox wrote . “Per Schultz, the Browns would prefer to get a third- or fourth-round pick in exchange for the receiver, though that may be difficult. “The 27-year-old struggled through last season and has fallen out of the game plan this year as Concepcion, Boston, and tight end Harold Fannin Jr. have become the go-to targets. Still, Jeudy is a talented pass-catcher who made the Pro Bowl just two years ago following a 1,229-yard season. His skill set hasn’t disappeared, and his 2026 base salary of $1.5 million should appeal to budget-conscious teams.” The Kansas City Chiefs have been pretty snake-bitten when it comes to keeping healthy wide receivers on their roster. Second-leading receiver Tyquan Thornton suffered a gruesome ankle injury nearly two weeks ago against the Las Vegas Raiders that will likely sideline him the rest of the season. Rashee Rice could miss some time with hamstring and knee injuries, and both Jeff Caldwell and Jimmy Holiday have been on injured reserve since the end of August. As things sit now, Xavier Worthy (14 catches, 133 yards, one touchdown), Jalen Royals (three catches, 17 yards, one TD), Cyrus Allen and Nikko Remigio are the only healthy WRs on Kansas City’s roster — and the latter two haven’t recorded a catch this season, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report thinks they should look to upgrade the position. Jeudy (eight catches for 81 yards in five games) has been almost a non-factor this season with the emergence of Boston and Concepcion. However, he had a 90-reception, 1,229-yard, four-TD season just two years ago. In Kansas City he would see much more than the three targets per game he’s currently getting in Cleveland. Jeudy would also give quarterback Patrick Mahomes the kind of reliable big-play target he’s been missing ever since the team traded away Tyreek Hill. home.blurb: Included in the list of injured players were starting left tackle Joe Alt (neck, DNP), star safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring, DNP) and leading wide receivers Ladd McConkey (foot, limited participant) and Quentin Johnston (chest, limited). At wide receiver, Los Angeles is dealing with a plethora of issues. (KCTV) - A wounded and winless Los Angeles Chargers team is headed toward Kansas City this weekend looking to hand the Chiefs their first loss of the season. But those aforementioned wounds are mounting after five weeks of play, and Wednesday’s injury report shared by head coach Jim Harbaugh’s team was a lengthy one. In total, nearly 40 percent of the Chargers’ active roster were listed with some ailment after their first practice of the week. Not included on the injury report was Chargers center Tyler Biadasz, who was placed on season-ending injured reserve in August due to a torn ACL suffered in training camp and starting right tackle Rashawn Slater and backup Trey Pipkins, who were each placed on injured reserve in recent weeks due to ankle and knee issues. As a result, last week, injuries on the Chargers offensive line led to multiple rookies starting for Los Angeles in a game where star quarterback Justin Herbert was sacked five times. All of those injuries to Chargers pass-catchers, which include tight end David Njoku being placed on injured reserve in September, resulted in the Chargers hosting several wide receivers for tryouts on Tuesday and signing former Raymore-Peculiar and KU alum Luke Grimm to their practice squad. Kansas City and Los Angeles kick off Sunday’s game at 3:25 p.m. CT. It can be watched live in Kansas City and the surrounding viewing area on KCTV5.
