picks.blurb: Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Bills vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 6 Tim Crean, ClutchPoints Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:44 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Buffalo Bills face off against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 6. This matchup between the 4-1 Bills and the 3-2 Raiders gets a prime spot in the late Sunday window as one of the best games of the week. These two original AFC franchises haven't played a game with meaningful stakes for both teams since the 1993 "Just Freeze Baby" Divisional Round game . Now, as both sides come into this game with winning records, let's make some bold Bills-Raiders predictions. Start your Raiders in fantasy football The Bills are their own worst enemy so far this season, as they love to gift their opponents chances to stay in the game. Whether it is shockingly cavalier Josh Allen interceptions, infuriating James Cook fumbles, or the fact that the defense (outside of Deone Walker and Gregory Rousseau) looks like it has no clue what it is doing right now, Buffalo loves keeping the other team in the game. Sunday will be no different, as fans should expect at least two turnovers from the Bills' offense and long stretches where the Raiders' O looks like the 2007 New England Patriots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That means big games from the Raiders' defense, Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers, Ashton Jeanty, and maybe even the likes of Mike Washington Jr., Michael Mayer, and Tre Tucker. So, for all you fantasy football players out there, any Raiders on your roster should be a good play in Week 6 . Josh Allen delivers again Despite the mediocre (or worse) play at times from the Bills' offensive line, wide receivers, tight end, and running backs, and defensive back seven, the Bills are 4-1 and leading the AFC East thanks to one man: Brandon Beane. Just kidding! He's the reason the rest of the team is struggling so much. The real reason is Josh Allen. Through five weeks, Allen is still the betting favorite for NFL MVP this year. Yes, Brock Bowers is playing great, and Patrick Mahomes is back, but if you define MVP as the players whose absence would tank his team's chances the most, Allen has to be the answer. Monday night's dramatic OT win over the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams came courtesy of 210 yards passing and a staggering 121 yards rushing from the Bills QB. Sure, he threw his obligatory head-scratching pick in the first half, but in the second, it was a one-man battle with 53 Rams players, and the singular man won. Against the Raiders, expect more of the same. Vegas has an improved defense this season and an incredible pass rusher in Maxx Crosby, but that only means Allen will be forced to take off even more as usual. And with his receivers getting minimal separation and Cook's suspect ball security, it will be all Allen, all the time in Week 6. Bills 31, Raiders 24 This won't be a cakewalk for the Bills by any means, as the Raiders are one of (if not) the most improved teams in the league. We know Cousins is a professional QB, the Raiders have some incredible young offensive weapons, and Klint Kubiak seems like a legit NFL head coach with an incredibly bright future. Allen doesn't have those last two things, as his skill position core is the exact same as last year, as long as D.J. Moore is out injured and his "new" head coach is just the same offensive coordinator who couldn't get it done the past three seasons, but with a more impressive title. Nevertheless, Allen should be able to will his Bills to victory over the Raiders in Week 6 just by sheer force of talent and will. As good as Las Vegas has looked at times this season, they are probably a year or two away from being legit contenders. That's why we'll take the Buffalo to win here, and to do so by slightly more than the -5.5-point spread suggests. Las Vegas could find more success through the air against a Buffalo defense that has repeatedly subjected the team to shootouts, but the Raiders might not have enough ammunition to come out on top. picks.blurb: NFL Week 6 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Another Packers-Cowboys clash, Raiders scare Bills Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites NHL Detroit Red Wings Boston Bruins Montreal Canadiens New Jersey Devils Chicago Blackhawks COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The unbeatable Los Angeles Rams superteam is now 2-3 on the 2026 NFL season. The Houston Texans just got their first win. The Dallas Cowboys can't get out of their own way, and the Buffalo Bills are mauling everyone in their way. It's been a wacky start to the season, which has made our NFL picks and predictions for every game each week a bit more difficult than I expected. We're having to adjust our perceptions and expectations on the fly, and we're still in the mix as we head into what should be a fascinating Week 6. Zach Rotman came out of the bullpen for me last week and came through with a solid week. Many, many thanks to him for helping the cause, but I'm back in the saddle now. Let's hope I don't make this thing go any further off the rails, but let's dive right into this fun slate with our NFL picks for Week 6 as we make predictions both straight-up and against the spread for all 14 games on the slate this week. NFL Week 6 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game NFL Week 6 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Seahawks vs. Broncos (TNF) Seahawks -2.5 Texans vs. Jaguars (London) Bears vs. Falcons Ravens vs. Browns Jets vs. Patriots Patriots -7.5 Saints vs. Giants Titans vs. Colts Panthers vs. Eagles Panthers +1.5 Steelers vs. Buccaneers Steelers -2.5 Cardinals vs. Rams Bills vs. Raiders Chargers vs. Chiefs Cowboys vs. Packers Commanders vs. 49ers 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 51-28 (Last week 9-6) | ATS Record: 37-40-2 (Last week 8-7) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 6 prediction to make Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders (+5.5) Buffalo Bills at Las Vegas Raiders (+5.5) The Buffalo Bills have been rolling, including toppling the Rams in overtime in Los Angeles on Monday night. Stop me if you've heard this one before, but Buffalo has one of the NFL's best offenses behind Josh Allen and it doesn't seem like there's a defense in the league that's going to be able to stop this team from scoring 30 points — they're quite literally averaging 32.7 points per game after the first five games of the year. Meanwhile, the Raiders have certainly fallen back to earth a bit, losing two straight after their 3-0 start to the season. At the same time, the Bills defense is the same problem it's been for the past few years. It seems like Buffalo has to produce at this level offensively to win games because the defense is going to give it up. While the Raiders might not be a surprise contender, they still look like a quite competent football team behind Kirk Cousins and, while Buffalo will be able to score on their defense, they're still averaging 26.4 points per game on the year. I think Buffalo still has the offensive firepower against a middling defense to get the win in this game. But with it being in Vegas against a team that has a legitimate pulse, it's going to be another shootout and one that could likely be decided by a field goal once again. 5.5 points is a bit too many, so we'll take the Raiders against the spread and pray. Easiest NFL Week 6 pick on the board Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5) This line could've been two touchdowns and I'm still taking the Kansas City Chiefs over the division rival Chargers. For starters, what has LA shown this season to make you believe they have a chance in Arrowhead in Week 6? No, seriously. There's been little evidence to think that this game will be close as the Chiefs have been absolutely rolling on both sides of the ball while Justin Herbert delivers the worst season of his career, the Chargers defense is middling at its best and the self-inflicted wounds in each game from LA multiply likes the heads of a hydra. If that weren't enough, Andy Reid is famously one of the most lethal head coaches when his team is coming off of the bye week. This isn't to say that the Chiefs are a perfect team as I maintain that they still need to find some more upgrades at wide receiver, especially after the gnarly Tyquan Thornton injury. While that may be true, though, they are a far better coached and more talented team than the winless Chargers and I wouldn't be surprised if this game was lopsided and out of hand early in favor of the home side. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Dallas Cowboys (+1.5) at Green Bay Packers Coming off of a home loss to undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels and the previously winless Buccaneers, naturally I'm taking the Dallas Cowboys to go on the road to Lambeau and beat the Packers as underdogs. What about this doesn't make sense to you? Yes, the optics look strange. However, this isn't about expecting the Cowboys hiring Mike Pettine to essentially help out new defensive coordinator Christian Parker drastically improving the defense, though it can't hurt. It's more about this being a likely shootout between these two teams because, despite what happened to Tyson Bagent and the Bears, I still don't trust Green Bay on that side of the ball. Furthermore, I also still don't trust the Packers run game, even against Dallas. Expect this game to go back and forth throughout the action, but I believe the Cowboys are going to have more offensive firepower and some adjustments on the side of the ball you can actually trust Dallas on to attack Green Bay throughout. They might not come up with many stops of their own, but they'll have enough to pull out the win. Plus, just from a narrative perspective, if ever there was a time for the Cowboys to keep their fans from abandoning ship, it's a game like this, and this franchise has been masterful at doing exactly that over the years. Buffalo is coming off its most impressive win of the season, beating the potent Los Angeles Rams in overtime, 37-34, in a Monday Night Football classic where win probabilities swung to and fro like the doors of an Old West saloon. The Raiders come into the game after a 45-17 loss to the New England Patriots led by QB Drake Maye. Even with the short week, Josh Allen and the Bills are the early favorites among NFL analysts. away.blurb: There were four new additions with starting right tackle Spencer Brown, rookie outside linebacker TJ Parker, safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson and running back Ty Johnson all apparently coming out of Monday's win bothered by injury. Brown, who was limited on Wednesday, is the name that warrants the most attention. The right tackle left Monday's win after only 16 snaps due to a back flare-up. If guys can be out there, the anticipation is for them to be out there," said head coach Joe Brady. Buffalo held a walkthrough practice on Wednesday at UC Irvine, meaning participation status is only an estimation. Five of the 15 players were listed as limited participants. Wide receiver DJ Moore and defensive lineman Ed Oliver, neither of whom were available in Week 5 , were the lone two non-participants. "Just tweaked it. Nothing major. Disc looks fine. Had an MRI. Looks better than it did last year. Long-term wise that's good to hear. It's [current issue] straight up just muscular freaking out," said Brown addressing reporters following the walkthrough. Along with Brown, Johnson was also limited on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Gardner-Johnson and Parker were full participants. Giving it a go in Weeks 3 and 4, Moore was finally forced to sit out in Week 5 after reaggravating the injury against the New England Patriots on October 4. It was the first time Moore missed a game since December 2020, ending a 91-game appearance streak. Meanwhile, Palmer injured his shoulder in practice last Friday. home.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown left Monday night's 37-34 victory over the Los Angeles Rams because of a back injury and did not return, adding another starter to Buffalo's list of health concerns. NFL teams have to submit a report on practice participation on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for a Sunday game. There are three levels of practice participation that can be designated: did not participate, limited participation and full participation. Bills athletic trainers tended to Brown on the field before he walked off under his own power. He appeared to grab at his back while walking toward the sideline and went directly into the blue medical tent. Brown later went to the locker room and did not return. Buffalo initially listed Brown as questionable before downgrading him to out during the fourth quarter. He was listed as questionable but did not play Monday. Oliver did not practice at all last week. Joshua Palmer was ruled out against the Rams after suffering a shoulder injury during Friday's practice. Palmer was not listed on Thursday's injury report before being limited Friday and sitting out Saturday. He was listed as questionable but was inactive against the Rams. Zane Durant is eligible to return after beginning the season on injured reserve. Buffalo can designate Durant to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is medically cleared. Tyrell Shavers is eligible to return after beginning the season on the physically unable to perform list. The Bills can designate him to return and open his 21-day practice window when he is ready. picks.blurb: Cowboys vs. Packers bold prediction for Week 6 Sunday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Cowboys vs. Packers bold prediction for Week 6 Sunday Night Football Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Wed, October 14, 2026 at 9:43 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys are two teams moving in opposite directions headed into Week 6. Dallas got schooled by Tampa Bay in Week 5 and their new-look defense has looked terrible for multiple games in a row. Their offensive production has also been streaky to say the least. Meanwhile, the Packers are riding a two-game winning streak and just beat the pulp out of the Bears at Lambeau Field . Green Bay will host Dallas at Lambeau once again in primetime this weekend. Packers fans will be out in full force and create a hostile environment for the Cowboys. But Dallas is absolutely desperate for a win, which means anything could happen in this game. So which team will come out on top in this one? And who will fans learn more about based on the game's result? Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Here are three bold predictions ahead of the Week 6 matchup between the Cowboys and Packers on Sunday Night Football. Dak Prescott, Jordan Love combined for over 750 passing yards in epic duel Jerome Miron-Imagn Images The offenses may be more important than the defenses in this game. There is a clear mismatch on paper when comparing the Packers and Cowboys defenses so far this season. But just a quick look at each offense shows that this game could easily become a shootout. Both the Cowboys and Packers are both top five teams this season in terms of passing yards per game. Green Bay averages 271.0 passing yards per game , with Dallas right behind them at 269.6. If two teams are going to get into a high-scoring slugfest, it would be these two. It's interesting that both teams are getting it done in different ways. Dallas has a duo of elite wide receivers in CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Meanwhile, the Packers are enjoying Christian Watson's breakout season that has unlocked the entire offense. Ultimately, this game could be decided by which quarterback has a better game. Prescott and Love will combine for more than 750 passing yards on Sunday Night Football. If split evenly, each quarterback would need at least 375 passing yards to make this happen. Obviously that would be a great game for each of them. Fans will fall in love with this game if there truly are this many fireworks. Javonte Williams has best game of the season against vulnerable Packers defense One area where the Cowboys have an advantage is the running game. The Packers have the worst rushing attack in football with just 60.4 yards per game this season. A combination of offensive line injuries and the lack of Josh Jacobs has completely neutralized this unit. Now the Cowboys aren't that much better on paper. They rank 30th in the league with 81.6 rushing yards per game. That doesn't sound like a big difference, but it is. The biggest reason to have confidence in the Dallas running game is Javonte Williams. He has been solid throughout the season, but has yet to have a truly special game in terms of rushing yards. In fact, he's yet to go over 100 rushing yards in a game this season. Dallas activated All-Pro guard Tyler Smith from injured reserve before last week's game. There's reason to believe he could make an impact on the ground, especially now that he's had a week to get settled. Williams gets his 100-yard rushing game against the Packers, bringing some much-needed stability to the Dallas offense. This could make the difference in this game, as Dallas is better positioned to control the clock if they can gain a lead in the second half. Cowboys win a close one-score game… thanks to a huge play by their defense Steven Bisig-Imagn Images The Cowboys invested a ton in their defense this offseason after last year's struggles. But they simply haven't looked up to the job so far in 2026. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones went out and hired Mike Pettine to help improve the defense alongside defensive coordinator Christian Parker. It may take some time before that addition actually moves the needle, if it does at all. But simply having a veteran coach in defensive meetings could improve one or two small things right away in Week 6. It doesn't take much for a terrible defense to improve. Look no further than the Lions, who still have the league's worst defensive unit. They stood up to the Cardinals with their backs against the wall in Week 5. It's not crazy to assume the Cowboys could pull off a similar case of positive regression. This entire game could tilt in Dallas' favor if they can just make a few big plays on defense. The Cowboys will win this game by making a big defensive play to seal this game. Think a decisive stop on a crucial fourth down or a game-winning turnover in the fourth quarter. picks.headline: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week
picks.blurb: Week 6 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys and Packers had much different results last week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 15, 2026 at 2:37 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads One week can change the entire perception of an NFL team — sometimes that's good, sometimes it's not. The Dallas Cowboys and Green Bay Packers were both 2-2 coming into last week's games. The Cowboys weren't considered a Super Bowl contender, but they were at least looking OK — especially in a bad NFC East — with a home game against the winless Buccaneers coming up. The Packers had played so poorly through four weeks that they were home underdogs to the Bears for the first time in 20 years , even though Chicago was starting its backup quarterback. The Cowboys and Packers come into Week 6's Sunday night game with their seasons flipped around. The Cowboys looked horrible against the Buccaneers, losing to an undrafted rookie quarterback in Jalon Daniels. The defensive problems finally got to a point in which the Cowboys hired longtime NFL defensive coordinator Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant and said defensive coordinator Christian Parker will now call plays from the press box. There's always some angst in Dallas because of the attention on the Cowboys all the time, but it's not like the defensive problems are made up. Dallas was last in defensive DVOA last season and they're last so far this season. Meanwhile, the talk of Matt LaFleur being on the hot seat seems like it was a lot longer than a week ago. The best way to gain back the confidence of Packers fans is to blow out the Bears, and the Packers did just that. They blasted Chicago, 31-7, with Jordan Love embarrassing the Bears defense with his deep passing and Green Bay shutting down everything Chicago's offense wanted to do. After not playing a good game through four weeks, the Packers played a great game in Week 5. That makes Week 6 hard to figure out. Do the Cowboys rebound or is the defense simply unfixable? What's the real Packers team — the one that couldn't run the ball, couldn't protect Love and had a below-average defense through four games, or the one we saw Sunday? The Packers are small favorites Sunday night, indicating the oddsmakers don't have a lot of confidence in them still. But it's tougher to bank on the Cowboys' defense. Packers -1.5 is the pick , though it could all look different for both teams next week. That's how the NFL goes. The Green Bay Packers' MarShawn Lloyd celebrates a touchdown with the fans at Lambeau Field last week. (AP Photo/Nam Huh) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 6 of the NFL season: Seahawks (-2.5) over Broncos Not all is great for the defending champs, who can't run the ball and still don't have an offensive option other than Jaxon Smith-Njigba. But they've been far better than the Broncos, who were on their way to losing to the winless and injury-plagued Chargers before saving themselves with a fourth-quarter rally. The matchup of Seattle's defense against an aimless Broncos offense is enough to take the Seahawks. Jaguars (-2.5) over Texans A bit of a weird line. The Jaguars are 4-1 and while last week's miracle win over the Eagles wasn't great, they do look like a legitimate contender in the AFC. The Texans are 1-4 and their lone win came against the 0-5 Titans. And yet, in a neutral site game — if either team has the edge it's Jacksonville, who does the London trip every season and stayed overseas after playing there last week — the Jaguars aren't even giving a full field goal. Yes it's a desperate Houston team with a very good defense, but it's not a lot of respect for the Jaguars. Falcons (+1.5) over Bears It appears Michael Penix Jr. and Caleb Williams will start, which should make for an entertaining game. The big question for this one will be what to make of the Bears defense. In Week 1 and 5 they gave up 68 combined points. From Weeks 2-4 they allowed 28 points. The hot stretch in the middle could have come from facing three bad offenses (Vikings without Kyler Murray in bad weather, Eagles, Jets) instead of the Panthers and Packers, their other two opponents who both scored more than 30 points. The Falcons are a good offense with Penix, so points should be coming. Browns (+5.5) over Ravens The Ravens should have confidence after beating the Falcons without Lamar Jackson last week. However, a Tyler Huntley offense still isn't one I'm comfortable laying 5.5 points with on the road. Buccaneers (+2.5) over Steelers Metrics like DVOA and net EPA per play say these teams are practically even. The Buccaneers have the rest advantage, having played last Thursday night, and the Steelers are 0-2 on the road (3-0 at home). Daniels could be exposed by the best defense he's faced, but it's also not the intimidating Steelers defense from recent years. Patriots (-7.5) over Jets The Patriots are officially warmed up. The start to the season was lackluster, but Drake Maye is coming off two good games in a row. The Jets are better than some expected, but they're facing a team that has its season back on track and wants to keep that going. Bet the New England Patriots to cover the spread at sportsbooks Giants (+1.5) over Saints It's hard to buy the Giants. There's no evidence they're a good team despite their 3-1-1 record. But it's not like there are any signs that the Saints are much better. New Orleans is 30th in DVOA ahead of only the hopeless Titans and Dolphins. Anything can happen when Jameis Winston is starting at quarterback, good or bad — good luck predicting it. Panthers (-1) over Eagles It's weird to see the Panthers favored at Philadelphia (though some books have the Eagles as a small favorite). But to this point, Carolina has been the far better team. Also, they're coming off a bye while the Eagles come right off a flight from London, where they took a horrific loss after kicking a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. Colts (-7) over Titans The Titans should be very happy the Dolphins exist, or else there would be even more talk about how bad they are. Indianapolis hasn't been great, either, but it's just too difficult to take the Titans right now. Cardinals (+12.5) over Rams It's quite possible the Rams take out their frustrations on the Cardinals. Los Angeles is 2-3, but the schedule has been tough and it starts to ease up with a game against Arizona, which just got throttled by the Lions. The Cardinals seem to be running out of steam after looking decent to start the season. Still, 12.5 points is a lot considering the Rams haven't looked great yet, and Arizona can move the ball, especially in garbage time. Raiders (+5.5) over Bills The Bills are coming off an emotional, difficult overtime win against the Rams on Monday night. They are the better team, but that's a tough situational spot, and the Raiders are not as bad as they looked last week against the Patriots. Let's give Vegas one more shot to show that 3-0 start wasn't fraudulent. Chiefs (-8) over Chargers The Chargers aren't just bad, they're injured. They held their own against the Broncos last week, but that probably says more about Denver. This season is already ugly for Los Angeles and it's not going to get much better. Commanders (+7.5) over 49ers If the Commanders aren't completely downtrodden after one of the dumbest endings in recent NFL history last week, in which they casually watched the final minute of overtime run out without getting a field-goal attempt, then this seems like too many points. The 49ers have played very well on both sides of the ball (the defense has been a great surprise), but there is some danger of a letdown after winning at Seattle. Take the points and hope last week's fiasco doesn't still linger for Washington. Last week: 5-9-1 Season to date: 34-43-2

away.headline: NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week
away.blurb: Caleb's return won't solve it all Now, to add insult to injury, the NFL is punishing two Cowboys players for their actions in Week 4 of the NFL season. Every weekend, the NFL sends out a report with its weekly punishments for holding players accountable for their actions during the prior week's games . NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL NFL punishes 2 Dallas Cowboys players, capping off a bad week Anne Erickson Sat, October 10, 2026 at 9:33 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Dallas Cowboys fell 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on "Thursday Night Football" to kick off the NFL's Week 5 festivities, and it wasn't a good look for the franchise. The main reason this loss was rough is because the Cowboys fell to a 0-4 Buccaneers team that has undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels subbing for the injured Baker Mayfield. You know something is wrong when you're losing to an undrafted free agent, but in all seriousness, Daniels was impressive. So, it could be more about his impressive showing than the Cowboys tanking, but still, this franchise is already on the clock to turn things around this season. Two Cowboys players fined by the NFL "Player infractions may come to the league's attention in a variety of ways. The league may respond to an official's call during a game or to a specific play that a team submits for review," the league notes. In this weekend's report, the NFL slaps Cowboys player Reddy Steward with a $5,583 fine for unnecessary roughness due to a hit on a defenseless player at 10:57 in the third quarter, as well as Kavontae Turpin with an $11,941 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct due to taunting at 10:50 in the third quarter. So, it's just a bit more bad news for two guys playing for a franchise that's hurting. But it's still early in the season, so the Cowboys have lots of time to come back. away.headline: Dallas Cowboys get important Micah Parsons injury update before trip to Green Bay to face the Packers
away.blurb: However, the latest injury update out of Green Bay suggests the Parsons vs. Dallas rematch may have to wait another year. “Packers are not anticipating that their standout pass rusher Mike Parsons will return to practice this week as Green Bay prepares for Sunday night's game versus Dallas Cowboys. There still is uncertainty about exactly when Parsons will return from his knee injury, but the hope still remains it will be this month.” To be fair, that alone does not rule Parsons out for Sunday night. But I find it hard to believe the Packers would risk a player they've invested so much in just to have him suit up against the Cowboys without practicing. The wording of Schefter's report matters too. If the hope is for Parsons to return at some point in October, it doesn't sound like Sunday against the Cowboys is the target date. Parsons is a problem to block, and the Cowboys know that better than anyone after watching him wreck opposing offenses early in his career. away.headline: Cowboys Injury Updates: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton, Joey Porter Jr.
away.blurb: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton Return After Injury Scares Lamb was hit on the same quad he took a hit to the week before, and it became painful, Schottenheimer said. Lamb exited with 8:32 remaining in the fourth quarter, was listed as questionable to return, and was back on the field on the same drive. He finished with 2 catches for 9 yards on 5 targets and played 34 of the Cowboys’ 60 offensive snaps. Cornerback DaRon Bland played all 72 defensive snaps with Porter out. “It affects us too much. A little bit, just missing a guy. You always wanna have everybody there, so. And to have a lot of guys hurt right now. So it hurts a little bit,” Bland said. “But we still had to go out there and perform.” Safety Alijah Clark left in the second quarter with a hamstring injury and was ruled out in the third quarter. Cornerback Shavon Revel was hurt on a third-quarter play and returned early in the fourth quarter. ‘Everything Still Out In Front Of Us’: Dallas Cowboys 1.5 Games Back As NFC East Goes Winless In Week 5 Cowboys Injury Updates: CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Guyton, Joey Porter Jr. Home ARLINGTON, Texas — Dallas Cowboys receiver CeeDee Lamb and left tackle Tyler Guyton both left Thursday night’s 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with injuries and returned, and cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was inactive after falling ill at AT&T Stadium. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer gave initial updates after the game. Four days earlier, Lamb set a career high with 17 catches for 189 yards and caught the go-ahead 12-yard touchdown with 40 seconds left in a 34-30 win over the Houston Texans . Guyton’s X-rays looked good, Schottenheimer said, but the Cowboys will run more tests on his back. Guyton played 52 offensive snaps, 87% of the total. Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones said he did not know the seriousness of Guyton’s back strain, but that Guyton came back in at the end. Joey Porter Jr. Becomes ‘Very, Very Sick’ Before Kickoff Porter was a late scratch, and Schottenheimer said the decision came after the trainers went to the coaches before the game. “Unique thing. Came to the stadium and he wasn’t feeling very well. And trainers came to us, said it got significantly worse after we treated him,” Schottenheimer said. “He just wasn’t feeling good. And the decision was made that he wasn’t going to be able to play, as he was very, very sick.” Jones said Porter had flu symptoms and could not keep his food down. Dallas acquired Porter in a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers last week, and Thursday was supposed to be his second game with the Cowboys, The Associated Press reported. DaRon Bland, Shavon Revel Among Cowboys Secondary Updates Receiver Jonathan Mingo was on the injury report entering the game, and Schottenheimer said a lot of people have had little things. Mingo played and caught 2 passes for 20 yards. Revel said after the game that he took a shot before kickoff and feels great. home.headline: Micah Parsons provides promising injury update for Packers fans
home.blurb: Micah Parsons, out since last December with a torn ACL, is nearing his comeback for the Packers as they look to bounce back from a slow start in the NFC North, winners of two games in a row. Around 9.5 months after his surgery last December, Parsons is nearing a return, but it won't come in Week 6 against his former Cowboys squad. He has yet to return to practice, and remains on Green Bay's PUP list as the team waits for him to be medically cleared. But it shouldn't be too long before that happens. "The biggest thing that people worried about with me, they're like, 'Man, why ain't he back yet?'" Parsons said. "If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl. But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first. What a lot of people don't figure out is it's not just the ACL. It's like, why did the ACL happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain. And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side." Previously, he said he thought a return to face the Cowboys in Week 6 was "realistic," but it won't materialize as hoped. It won't be long before one of the NFL's premiere pass rushers is back on the field. Parsons provided the latest update on his timeline on his podcast recently, saying he's in the final stages of making sure his knee will hold up. Here's what Parsons said about his injury outlook. MORE: The Sporting News' latest 2027 NFL Mock Draft Micah Parsons provides injury update Parsons said on the latest episode of his podcast, "The Edge With Micah Parsons," that if it was a do-or-die game, he'd be ready to play, but has preferred to play it safe with his longer timeline. The star pass rusher said he wants to make sure he's fully at 100% before he returns. "It's like, what's the point of getting me back for four weeks and then next thing you know, my groin [is] bothering me," Parsons said. "So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was," Parsons said on his podcast. "It's just another 'Sunday Night Football' game between two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's gonna want to be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just want to be healthy again. That's it." For now, Parsons is waiting to be cleared so he can begin his ramp up to play. It won't be happening this week, but soon, the Packers will be getting a game-changing weapon back for their defense. picks.blurb: Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Brewers take 3-0 NLCS lead Bats stun Snell, Dodgers Caleb's return won't solve it all Fantasy Basketball Draft Kit Commanders vs. 49ers bold predictions for Week 6 Monday Night Football Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints Wed, October 14, 2026 at 1:54 AM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads While the Washington Commanders are likely playing with a lame-duck coach, the San Francisco 49ers will be without a key defender. These teams, going in different directions, will meet in Week 6 on Monday Night Football, and here are bold predictions for the contest. Still reeling from a last-second overtime mental meltdown in the 27-27 tie to the Giants, the Commanders carry a record of 1-3-1 and a heavy underdog role into this game. Meanwhile, the 49ers are flying high with a record of 5-0 on the season. They're coming off an exciting 32-29 win over the Seahawks, giving them firm control of the NFC West title chase. 49ers QB Brock Purdy will throw for 300 yards The Commanders have been good against the run this season, giving up only 95.4 yards per game. They will have a challenge against the 49ers' offense, who are No. 8 in rushing yards per game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Look for the Commanders to slow, not stop, Christian McCaffrey. However, that opens things up for the 49ers' passing attack to hit high gear. The biggest problem the Commanders will have is Mike Evans. That's not a deep analysis. It's something every team faces when playing the 49ers. Purdy said Evans makes a big difference , according to ESPN. "He's a game changer," Purdy said after the win over the Seahawks. "True X receiver that, if you get the right look and stuff and you give him a chance, he can make defenses pay. "I thought today he did a great job with that, going up and getting the ball multiple times and just using his length and everything to create some separation. So as a quarterback, any time I have an (opportunity) to go to him, it always feels good." Evans doesn't shy away from the attention. And why should he? He's a future Hall of Famer. "I do feel like I'm one of the best receivers in the game," Evans said. "I got a big frame, so if you throw it around me, I'm going to do my best to try to make those contested grabs." The 49ers won't have Deebo Samuel, who suffered a hamstring injury against the Seahawks. That could allow the Commanders to focus more attention on Evans. But the 49ers still have threats, including George Kittle. And even Kittle has major respect for Evans, according to a post on X. "Mike Evans is really good at football," Kittle posted. 49ers TE George Kittle will have a season-high reception total Kittle's best game came in Week 3 against the Cardinals as he grabbed six passes for 82 yards and a pair of scores. Look for him to have a similar line against the Commanders with Samuel on the shelf. The 49ers have Kittle, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, and Jacob Cowing on the roster. And that's enough , said head coach Kyle Shanahan, according to ESPN. "I think we have enough," Shanahan said. "We've got three guys on practice squad also who can help. I mean, anytime you lose this number of guys, whether it's four guys or five guys, whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But we do have guys in this building who can do it, and we'll always look." Commanders QB Jayden Daniels will finally cross 200-yard passing mark In three games this season, Daniels hasn't totaled over 200 yards passing. Look for that to change against the 49ers. It makes sense for the 49ers to focus defensively on keeping Daniels in check as a runner. He's coming off a game where he ran for 103 yards on nine carries and a pair of touchdowns. And look for the Commanders' game plan to lean more on the passing game than it has so far this season. Part of it will likely be from necessity as the Commanders figure to be chasing points throughout this game. Daniels has a lot to prove after his late-game blunder against the Giants. He has tried to own the situation , according to ESPN. "We have to stop the clock," Daniels said. "We have to know the situation. We have to relay that as an offense. It starts with everyone, top down. Ultimately, it's on me." A bounce-back game against the 49ers by Daniels won't help Quinn's future as head coach. But it would be an olive branch to Commanders' fans who are furious about Daniels' mental meltdown. Commanders WR Terry McLaurin will get a long TD Look for the Commanders to strike deep against the 49ers. McLaurin should be the beneficiary with a 40-plus-yard score. McLaurin hasn't been anything special from a fantasy perspective this season. He had catch totals of 2, 2, 6, and 4 in his first four games. He has 203 total yards and one touchdown. Those aren't WR1 numbers. He is playing like a pedestrian blob so far this season. And while he probably won't juice up those numbers much against the 49ers' tough defense, it's not out of the realm of possibility for him to get a deep ball. How big of an ask is a 40-yard TD strike between Daniels and McLaurin? Consider that Daniels' longest pass of the season is 33 yards. McLaurin's longest catch is 30 yards. Those numbers seem to belie the likelihood of a long hookup. However, the 49ers can't fear the deep ball because of this duo's modest production. And that's why there's a window of opportunity for a bomb. However, look for the Commanders to fall to 1-4-1 after this one. They don't have the roster to compete with the 49ers. By Michael Gallagher Sports Content Coordinator 0 Share Newsweek is a Trust Project member See more of our trusted coverage when you search. Prefer Newsweek on Google to see more of our trusted coverage when you search. The San Francisco 49ers have had arguably the worst injury luck of any team in the NFL this season. More than 15 players are currently on the reserve/injured list while a handful of others are expected to miss some time with their respective ailments. San Francisco’s defense has been hit particularly hard, and star edge-rusher Nick Bosa’s absence over the last few weeks has been noticeable. Keion White has done his part to pick up the slack, but the rest of San Francisco’s pass-rush has left much to be desired, which is why Kristopher Knox of Bleacher Report believes the 49ers should make an all-in move to upgrade the position. Knox recently suggested the 49ers execute a trade with the winless Los Angeles Chargers for Pro Bowler Khalil Mack. “Los Angeles fell to 0-5 on Sunday, while Mack continues to be a legitimate difference-maker,” Knox wrote . “… Mack is playing on a one-year deal and should be interested in playing for a team that could get him his first career playoff win. “.. Mack should be the top target for any team with Super Bowl aspirations that happens to need help rushing opposing passers. It'll be a fairly significant surprise if he remains in Los Angeles beyond next month's deadline.” Despite multiple reports indicating the Chargers would want a fifth-round pick in exchange for Mack, Knox suggested it could take at least a conditional 2027 fourth-round pick to get a deal finalized given the demand for strong pass-rushers from contending teams. Through five games this season, Mack has logged 14 pressures, eight hurries, five tackles for loss, three QB hits, and three sacks with a pass-rush win-rate of 9.5%, according to Pro Football Focus. Adding that kind of production opposite White would be a big boost for the 49ers in the interim, and once Bosa comes back, it would make SF’s pass-rush all the more dangerous come playoff time.

It is time to simply enjoy what the 49ers are doing and stop worrying about their ability to stay healthy. Frankly, they might just win the Super Bowl regardless of who is available. Through five weeks, it feels like their year. Here is how the rest of the Super Bowl race shakes out as the season approaches Week 6. Stock down: Bears desperately await Caleb Williams' return Would the Chicago Bears be 5-0 if Caleb Williams did not get hurt in Week 2? Suppose he stays on the field for that critical fourth-quarter drive in the 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. He would have had at least two more looks at the end zone. If he were available in Week 5, the Bears probably would not throw three interceptions in a 31-7 rout at the hands of the bitter rival Green Bay Packers . That is all hypothetical, of course, but Williams' talent makes it fair to wonder. Instead, the Bears are two games back of the NFC North lead and stand in the middle of the conference's slog of three-win teams. The good news (and Chicago needs some right now) is that Williams is on track to play in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons .
